title: Longitudinal Eval Anchoring and Label Cost Optimizer
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This document describes the Longitudinal Eval Anchoring and Label Cost Optimizer (LEALCO), a pragmatic system and playbook for maintaining high-fidelity evaluation coverage over time while minimizing human labeling cost. LEALCO combines anchored reference slices, multi-fidelity probes, telemetry-driven resampling, and a lightweight optimizer that allocates labeling budget across slices. The playbook is intended for evaluation engineers, annotator stewards, and applied ML owners responsible for model promotion decisions.

Scope

- Applies to production and pre-production evaluation workflows across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Covers slice definition, anchor selection, probe generation, sampling cadence, labeling budget allocation, and promotion thresholds.
- Integrates with the eval harness, telemetry pipeline, and the annotation platform.

Definitions

- Anchor: a small, curated set of high-quality examples that represent a slice's ground-truth behavior across time (10–200 examples per slice depending on criticality).
- Probe: an automatically generated or instrumented example used for routine evaluation (low-cost, high-frequency).
- Slice: semantically coherent subset of workload (e.g., long-context summarization, non-English queries, code-generation with API calls).
- Fidelity: the annotation / evaluation effort level (micro, standard, deep).

Motivation

Teams repeatedly face two problems: (1) drift in model behavior across time and model variants, and (2) rapidly rising annotation costs when trying to preserve coverage. LEALCO trades off frequency versus fidelity: frequent low-cost probes detect shifts; anchors provide longitudinal stability for regression detection; and a cost optimizer decides which probes get escalated to full labels. This reduces false positives and labeling spend while preserving guardrail quality.

Design Principles

1. Anchoring first: every slice must have an immutable anchor snapshot stored in the eval catalog and treated as the longitudinal reference.
2. Multi-fidelity sampling: prefer many cheap probes (auto-labeled or heuristically checked) and escalate only when risk or divergence exceeds thresholds.
3. Telemetry-driven adaptivity: use production telemetry (latency, token usage, confidence, rerank scores) to prioritize slices for higher-fidelity labeling.
4. Budget-aware optimization: explicit monthly labeling budget per product with an optimizer that maximizes expected regression detection power.
5. Explainability: every allocation decision must be accompanied by the expected delta in detection power and cost estimate.

Anchoring Procedure (operational)

1. Slice creation
   - Owner proposes a slice with: name, short description, anchor size, default fidelity, and criticality tier (P0,P1,P2).
   - Example: slice=non_en_long_context; anchor_size=50; criticality=P1.
2. Anchor selection
   - Prefer human-curated examples that: cover edge-cases, include real user telemetry traces, and have stable ground-truth annotations.
   - Store anchors in the eval catalog with immutable id: anchor://<slice>/<version>/<sha>.
3. Anchor maintenance cadence
   - P0: quarterly review and re-anchor if >10% of anchor examples show annotation ambiguity.
   - P1: biannual review.
   - P2: annual review.
4. Versioning
   - Anchors are versioned separately from probe sets; promotions reference anchor version.

Sampling and Budgeting

- Sampling modes: random, telemetry-weighted, entropy-weighted, adversarial-augmented.
- Default cadence: daily probes x 200 samples per slice for P0; weekly x 1k for P1; monthly x 5k for P2 (tunable).
- Budget allocation algorithm (high level):
  1) Compute risk score per slice = w1*drift_metric + w2*telemetry_spike + w3*anchor_delta.
  2) Compute marginal detection value per unit label for each slice using historical variance and effect size estimates.
  3) Greedy allocate labels to slices ordered by marginal value until budget exhausted; reserve 10% for emergency investigations.

Label Cost Optimizer (algorithmic spec)

- Inputs: current probe signals, past detection rates, label cost per fidelity tier (micro=$0.10, standard=$0.75, deep=$4.00), monthly budget B.
- Objective: maximize expected number of true regression detections subject to cost(B) <= budget.
- Approximation: treat each slice as an independent Bernoulli detector with detection probability p(n) as a function of labels n; use diminishing returns curve p(n)=1-(1-beta)^n where beta estimated from historical sensitivity.
- Output: allocation table {slice -> {n_micro, n_standard, n_deep}} and expected detection uplift.

Telemetry and Metrics

Track the following per-slice time series (minimum 90-day retention at 1d granularity):

- probe_count: number of probes executed
- probe_failure_rate: fraction of probes that fail heuristics
- anchor_discrepancy: fraction of anchors mismatched vs baseline model
- label_cost_spent: USD per slice per period
- detection_latency: median time from probe anomaly to human-verified regression
- false_positive_rate: annotations flagged as non-regressions after escalation

Telemetry-driven triggers (examples):
- Escalate to standard labels if probe_failure_rate > 3% for 72 hours.
- Escalate to deep labels if anchor_discrepancy > 5% and telemetry_spike > 2x baseline.

Promotion and Gate Criteria

- Slice-level promotion threshold (example):
  - Stability pass: 7-day rolling anchor_discrepancy < 1% and probe_failure_rate < 0.5%.
  - Quality gate for model promotion: no P0 slice with anchor_discrepancy > 3% in last 30 days; at most one P1 slice > 5% with mitigation plan.

Operational Runbook: Step-by-step

1. Daily monitoring
   - Eval pipeline posts daily digest to #eval-alerts with top-10 highest risk slices.
   - Oncall reviewer inspects top-3 slices and approves optimizer run.
2. Optimizer execution (weekly)
   - Run: pipeline: eval-harness/optimizer/run --date $(date -d 'yesterday' +%F) --budget 2000
   - Verify output allocation and expected uplift in CI.
   - Submit label orders to annotation platform and tag tasks with "lealco_alloc".
3. Post-labeling validation
   - Aggregate labels, compute updated detection metrics, and compare expected vs observed uplift.
   - Update slice sensitivity estimates (beta) using Bayesian update (Beta-Bernoulli).
4. Emergency investigation (ad-hoc)
   - Reserve 10% monthly budget. To trigger, create a JIRA ticket and tag severity.

Configuration Table (example)

| config_key | default | description |
|------------|---------|-------------|
| monthly_label_budget_usd | 5000 | Monthly labeling budget for the product team |
| reserve_fraction | 0.10 | Fraction of budget reserved for emergencies |
| p0_anchor_size | 50 | Anchor size for P0 slices |
| probe_cadence_P0 | daily | Probe execution cadence |
| fidelity_costs | micro:0.10,standard:0.75,deep:4.00 | Per-label costs used by optimizer |

Example CLI/JSON outputs

- Optimizer run command:
  eval-ops run-optimizer --project payments --budget 3000 --env prod --out allocations.json

- allocations.json (sample):
  {
    "slice": "non_en_long_context",
    "allocate": {"n_standard": "120", "n_micro": "300"},
    "expected_detection_uplift": "0.42",
    "estimated_cost_usd": "210.00"
  }

Integration points

- Eval harness: plug-in hook optimizer.adapt_allocation(...) called weekly.
- Annotation platform: tasks must be tagged with lealco_alloc and slice id.
- Telemetry: uses /telemetry/eval-probes and /telemetry/anchors endpoints.
- Promo dashboard: displays slice-level metrics and pending allocations.

Ownership and Roles

- Evaluation Engineers: maintain slice definitions and sensitivity estimates.
- Annotation Steward: manage labeling tasks, QA, and cost reconciliation.
- Product ML Owner: approve monthly budget and emergency releases.
- Oncall Reviewer: 1-week rotation in the eval team to triage alerts.

Rollout Plan

1. Pilot (4 weeks)
   - Select 5 P0/P1 slices across product lines; budget $2k; run optimizer weekly.
   - Measure detection uplift and labeling cost accuracy.
2. Scale (3 months)
   - Expand to 20 slices; integrate with promotion gating.
3. Org-wide adoption (6 months)
   - Add dashboarding, automatic tag propagation, and per-team budgets.

Failure modes and mitigations

- Optimizer overfits to historical sensitivity estimates -> Mitigate by capping maximum allocation per slice (30% of budget) and enforcing exploration samples.
- Anchors rot (stale examples) -> Mitigate with scheduled anchor audits and a checksum-based hash to detect drift in annotation patterns.
- Sudden telemetry outage -> Mitigate with conservative fallback allocations (equal-per-slice) until telemetry is restored.

Appendix A: Example anchor metadata schema (YAML)

anchor_id: anchor://non_en_long_context/v3/sha256:abcd1234
slice: non_en_long_context
created_by: "Maya Chen"
created_at: "2024-11-05"
examples_count: 50
notes: |
  - Selected to maximize language diversity and include long-context truncation cases.

Appendix B: Quick checklist for evaluators

- [ ] Confirm anchor existence and version in eval catalog.
- [ ] Verify telemetry spikes are real (check raw logs).
- [ ] Run optimizer and review allocations.
- [ ] Approve label tasks and tag with lealco_alloc.
- [ ] Validate post-label uplift and update sensitivity estimates.
